summary.text: D. Adam Smith is the Democratic incumbent for Washington's 9th Congressional District. A lawyer and former Seattle city prosecutor, he was elected to the Washington State Senate at age 25 and to Congress in 1996, taking office in 1997. He is the Ranking Member of the House Armed Services Committee and chaired the committee in the 116th and 117th Congresses.

paragraphs.text: Smith was born June 15, 1965, in Washington, D.C., and raised in SeaTac, Washington, graduating from Tyee High School in 1983.

He attended Western Washington University for a year, then graduated from Fordham University in 1987 with a degree in political science, and earned a law degree from the University of Washington in 1990.

According to his official biography, he worked as a lawyer at Cromwell, Mendoza and Belur beginning in 1992 and as a prosecutor for the City of Seattle from 1993 to 1995, focusing on drunk driving and domestic violence cases.

Smith won election to the Washington State Senate in 1990 from the 33rd Legislative District, defeating a 16-year incumbent; his official biography says he was 25 when he took office in January 1991. He was re-elected in 1994 and served on the Education and Law and Justice Committees, chairing Law and Justice from 1993 to 1997.
He was elected to the U.S. House in 1996 and assumed office in January 1997.

Smith has served on the House Armed Services Committee since entering Congress. He previously chaired its Air and Land Forces subcommittee and its Terrorism, Unconventional Threats and Capabilities subcommittee, and also served on the Foreign Affairs and Intelligence Committees.
Smith chaired the full Armed Services Committee in the 116th and 117th Congresses (2019-2022) and is its Ranking Member in the 119th Congress.
He co-founded the bipartisan Congressional Caucus for Effective Foreign Assistance, and a 2020 news report also lists him as a member of the Council on Foreign Relations.
According to his official biography, he married Sara Bickle-Eldridge in 1993, and they have two children.
